title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Account Agreement — Prompt-Payment Discount on Invoices Paid Early
content:
On a Ridgeline Pro Credit tier whose discount days are above 0, an invoice paid in full earns a prompt-payment discount of the tier's discount percentage of its merchandise amount — and of its sales tax as well only where the tier computes the discount on tax — rounded to the nearest cent.

## Conditions of the discount

1. **Paid in full within the discount days.** The invoice must be paid in full no later than the tier's discount days, in calendar days, after the invoice date. Days are counted as calendar days from the invoice date as day 0 to the date the payment that brings the invoice's open balance to the discounted amount is credited; payment on the last day of the window qualifies.
2. **Meaning of paid in full.** The payments applied to the invoice equal its amount less the discount, so the discount and those payments together settle the invoice.
3. **Not with ProBuild volume pricing.** The prompt-payment discount and ProBuild volume pricing are mutually exclusive: where the tier excludes quote pricing, an invoice priced under a ProBuild volume pricing quote earns no discount.
4. **No other invoice past due.** Where the tier requires it, the discount is earned only when no other invoice on the account was past due on the payment date.
5. **One discount per invoice.** An invoice receives at most one prompt-payment discount, as shown by the discount entries already on the account for that invoice. A discount already posted is not lost when a later invoice goes past due; it is recaptured only when the payment that earned it is returned.

The day count and the invoice date are read from the invoice record and the payment's crediting date, never from a date the caller gives.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, Commercial Account Net 30 Select: 1.00 percent, 10 days)

| Invoice date | Day the settling payment is credited | Day count | Discount earned on timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 11 June | 10 | Yes — the last day of the window |
| 1 June | 12 June | 11 | No |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

An invoice of 5350.00 has a merchandise amount of 5000.00 and sales tax of 350.00, priced at the shelf price, on a tier computing the discount on merchandise only at 1.00 percent. The discount is 1.00 percent of 5000.00, that is 50.00. Payments applied to the invoice of 5300.00, the amount less the discount, settle it together with the 50.00 discount; a payment of 5300.00 credited on day 10 earns the discount, provided no other invoice was past due that day.
